channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: New Modern Clinic Opens in Almaty Region's Raimbek District
item.description: A new modern clinic capable of serving 250 patients per shift has opened in the village of Narynkol, the administrative center of the Raimbek district in the Almaty region. The facility, costing 4.1 billion tenge, is equipped with advanced medical equipment and will improve healthcare quality in the mountainous region.

item.title: 90th Anniversary Celebrated for Zylikha Tamshybay, Hero of Socialist Labor
item.description: The 90th birthday of Zylikha Tamshybay, a Hero of Socialist Labor renowned for transforming the 'Enbekshi' state farm, was celebrated in her home village. The event included laying wreaths at her bust, an exhibition of her life and work, and a scientific conference attended by the regional governor.

item.title: Taliban Arrest Three More Residents in Panjshir Amid Intensified Crackdown
item.description: The Taliban have arrested three more residents from Panjshir's Abdullah Khil Valley in connection with a vehicle explosion targeting their fighters. This follows an earlier wave of detentions, bringing the total arrested to at least 27. Sources report increased harassment of locals by newly deployed Taliban units.

item.title: Former Hotel Owned by Nazarbayev's Nephew Sold in Almaty on Third Attempt
item.description: A former hotel, previously owned by the nephew of Kazakhstan's ex-president Nursultan Nazarbayev, has been sold in Almaty. The sale was successfully concluded on the third attempt, indicating previous difficulties in finding a buyer for the property.

item.title: Pentagon Urges European Allies to Soften Rhetoric Towards Russia
item.description: Pentagon officials have asked NATO allies to reduce sharp statements about the threat from Russia, according to Reuters. The US Department of Defense believes such rhetoric can provoke tension and harm European security. Some allies, like Estonia, have rejected the call for restraint.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Amends Rules for Energy Certification of Buildings
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has introduced changes to the procedure for energy certification of buildings, as per a resolution signed by the Cabinet of Ministers chairman. The amendments update regulations on energy efficiency assessment, introducing scales from A to G for various energy consumption indicators, including heating and hot water usage.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Nearly 20% Drop in Inmate Population Due to Probation
item.description: The introduction of a probation mechanism in Kyrgyzstan has led to a nearly 20% reduction in the number of inmates. The Ministry of Justice reported that the recidivism rate among individuals on probation is approximately 1%. The EU-funded 'Justice for All' project is supporting these reforms, including the development of a digital criminal justice ecosystem.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tax Reform Aims for Predictability and Efficiency in Business Environment
item.description: Kazakhstan's tax reform aims to create a more transparent, predictable, and modern digital system for businesses, moving beyond just reducing inspections. The reform acknowledges past moratorium experiences and emphasizes ensuring legal compliance while protecting citizens' interests. The goal is to foster an environment where businesses can thrive without excessive administrative hurdles.

item.title: Construction begins on new multi-profile hospital in Almaty
item.description: Construction has commenced on a new multi-profile hospital in Almaty, featuring a diagnostic center for 350 outpatients and a 250-bed oncology center. This development is crucial for the growing population of approximately 2.4 million. The complex is slated for completion in 2028.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President outlines path for a just and secure nation
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address to the nation sets forth key priorities for Kazakhstan's new stage of development, focusing on constitutional reforms. The agenda includes improving governance, economic growth, infrastructure modernization, and enhancing the investment climate, all aimed at raising living standards.

item.title: Poland's President returns amid escalating constitutional court crisis
item.description: Poland is facing a severe political and judicial crisis centered on a dispute between Prime Minister Donald Tusk's government and President Andrzej Duda concerning the Constitutional Tribunal. Protests erupted in Warsaw as a judge attempted to suspend tribunal leadership, leading to clashes with police.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Speaker Meets Public Representatives to Discuss National Development Goals
item.description: Erlan Koshanov, Chairman of the People's Council of Kazakhstan, met with public representatives in Akmola region. The discussion focused on implementing the President's Address regarding Kazakhstan's priorities in a new historical period. Koshanov highlighted reforms in politics and economics, and social infrastructure upgrades, noting significant investment in the social sector and job creation.

item.title: Police Investigate Suspected Suicide of Court Employee in Kokshetau
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Akmola region have opened a criminal case into the suspected suicide of a court employee in Kokshetau. The man's body was found on October 30. This is the second recent case of a court system employee's death by suicide in the region.

item.title: Bishkek Court Denies Activist Home Arrest Again
item.description: The Leninsky District Court in Bishkek has again rejected a request for home arrest for activist Tilekmat Kudaibergen uulu. His lawyer cited legal limits on pre-trial detention, noting the case has been ongoing for over a year. The judge denied the request, keeping him in pre-trial detention.

item.title: Kremlin Unaware of Plans for US, Russia, Ukraine Leaders' Meeting
item.description: The Kremlin stated it has no knowledge of any plans for a trilateral meeting involving the leaders of the United States, Russia, and Ukraine. US President Donald Trump had previously mentioned such a meeting, suggesting progress in US-Russia-Ukraine relations.

item.title: Tajik Citizens in Russian Prison Allege Forced Military Contracts
item.description: Tajik citizens serving sentences in a Volgograd prison claim they are being pressured by staff to sign contracts with the Russian Ministry of Defense. They have appealed to Dushanbe to be transferred back to their homeland, stating they are "left to die here."

item.title: Uzbek President Attends Turkic States Summit in Turkey
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Turkey from October 29-30, 2026, to attend the summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Ankara. The summit, themed 'Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Action,' focused on expanding trade, investment, transport, and digital cooperation among member states.

item.title: Uzbek-Polish Business Forum to Strengthen Trade and Economic Ties in Tashkent
item.description: A business forum between Uzbekistan and Poland will be held in Tashkent on November 4th to enhance trade and economic relations, expand business cooperation, and explore new joint project opportunities. Organized with the participation of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Uzbekistan, it aims to foster direct dialogue between business circles of both nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan and US Discuss Medical Cooperation; Polish Universities Sign MoUs
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Minister of Health met with a US delegation to discuss expanding medical cooperation, focusing on early disease diagnosis and maternal/child health. Separately, Polish medical university rectors visited Tashkent State Medical University, signing memorandums of understanding for joint research and academic exchange.

item.title: Turkmenistan Official Calls for Accurate and Reliable Media Reporting at Ankara Forum
item.description: Annasakhet Kakayev, Deputy Chairman of Turkmenistan's State Committee for Television, Radio Broadcasting, and Cinematography, spoke at a media forum in Ankara. He emphasized the importance of accuracy and reliability in news dissemination to foster trust and mutual respect among nations. Kakayev proposed five areas for developing information cooperation among Turkic states.

item.title: Turkmen President Meets with Turkish President in Turkey
item.description: Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow held a meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Turkey as part of his working visit. The leaders discussed strengthening bilateral relations in political, trade-economic, and cultural-humanitarian spheres. President Berdimuhamedow also extended greetings from the National Leader of the Turkmen people.

item.title: Turkmen President Addresses 13th Summit of Turkic States
item.description: Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow addressed the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States, expressing gratitude for the invitation and hospitality. He conveyed greetings from National Leader Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow and congratulated Turkey on Republic Day. The President emphasized Turkmenistan's commitment to strengthening ties within the Turkic world.

item.title: Dockworkers in 22 Countries Strike Against Arms Shipments
item.description: Dockworkers in over 100 ports across 22 countries are striking to protest the use of their ports for arms shipments and to commemorate sailors lost in conflicts. The strike, initiated by unions in Italy, France, Greece, Spain, Turkey, and Morocco, aims to halt the flow of military cargo. Participants also demand better wages and working conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Document Achieves UN Official Document Status
item.description: The final document of the 5th Samarkand Forum on Human Rights, titled 'Samarkand Vision – 2040: Global Cooperation for Human Dignity, Equality, and Sustainable Development,' has been granted official document status by the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. This designation underscores the forum's authority and facilitates the implementation of its decisions globally.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Enhance Judicial Cooperation
item.description: The Chairman of the Supreme Court of Uzbekistan, Robakhon Mahmudova, met with the Ambassador of Azerbaijan, Rashad Mammadov, to discuss reforms in the judicial system. Both sides emphasized the importance of strengthening bilateral relations and cooperation between judicial bodies, including within the framework of the Organization of Turkic States.

item.title: Germany and Ukraine Cooperate on New Armed Ground Robot Development
item.description: German company ARX Robotics and Ukrainian Roboneers have tested an armed ground robot for frontline use. The 'Gereon' platform will feature a 'Saber' remote weapon module, with the first systems expected by late 2026. The robot performs reconnaissance, cargo transport, casualty evacuation, and drone combat, and can be remotely operated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Turkey Discuss Development of Air Cargo Transportation
item.description: The Director of Kyrgyzstan's Civil Aviation Agency met with the Turkish Ambassador to discuss civil aviation cooperation. The ambassador congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its aviation successes, including removal from the European safety list. Discussions focused on current and future passenger and cargo air transport, including operations of Turkish Airlines and Asman Airlines.

item.title: Teenager Hospitalized After Electrocution on Train in Akmola Region
item.description: A 15-year-old boy in the Akmola region was electrocuted after climbing onto a train car. He sustained severe burns to approximately 70% of his body and is in critical condition. A criminal case has been initiated regarding the incident.

item.title: Uzbekistan's First Lady Addresses Women's Council on Education and Entrepreneurship
item.description: First Lady Ziroat Mirziyoyeva participated in the first meeting of the Turkic States Council of Family and Women. In her speech, she put forward initiatives aimed at expanding girls' access to modern education and developing women's entrepreneurship.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz Denies Offering to Reacquire Fergana Refinery After Privatization
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz has not proposed taking back the Fergana Oil Refinery into its structure after its return to state ownership. The refinery was transferred to the State Assets Management Agency in 2018 and subsequently privatized. Currently, the agency is exploring various management options for the facility, including potential return to Uzbekneftgaz or attracting new investors.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Limit Electricity for Water Debtors from 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Uzbekistan will change its procedures for collecting debts for drinking water and sewage services. The "Uzsuvtaminot" company announced that customers with outstanding water bills will face restrictions on their electricity payments. Debtors will receive a five-day notice to pay before services are limited and enforcement measures are taken.

item.title: Second Court Employee Found Dead in Kokshetau; Previous Death Under Investigation
item.description: The body of a second court employee has been found in Kokshetau, with preliminary information suggesting suicide. This follows the earlier discovery of a colleague's body. An investigation is underway to determine the circumstances surrounding both deaths. Social media reports suggest a possible link between the two incidents, involving a dispute between the deceased and two judges.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Financial Regulator Proposes Action Plan for Illegal Online Casinos
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's financial regulator proposed establishing total control over internet traffic to restrict access to illegal online casinos and other undesirable resources. He clarified that the aim is not to limit internet access for citizens, but to curb participation in illegal foreign gambling platforms.

item.title: Atyrau Oblast Accelerates Sewerage System Development Program
item.description: Atyrau Oblast is accelerating its sewerage system development program with a new roadmap and working group. Discussions focused on new network construction, infrastructure upgrades, and securing additional funding. Seven projects are planned for 2027, with further expansion in 2028 and subsequent phases covering multiple districts and areas.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Turkey's Feud Deepens Over Disagreements Regarding Israel
item.description: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev's absence from the Organization of Turkic States summit in Ankara signals a deepening feud with Turkish leader Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The dispute, initially centered on Azerbaijan's religious expression regulations, appears more complex than previously understood, embarrassing Erdogan and undermining his message of Turkic unity.

item.title: Central Asia's Power Grid Faces Winter Stress Amidst Rising Demand
item.description: Concerns are mounting in Central Asia regarding the region's capacity to meet electricity demand this winter, particularly in Kyrgyzstan, where cold weather has increased consumption. A Eurasian Development Bank study highlighted the fragility of the power grid, noting frequent overloads and bottlenecks that limit capacity during critical hours.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Bahrain Discuss Expanding Trade and Economic Cooperation
item.description: The second round of political consultations between Kazakhstan and Bahrain took place in Manama. The parties discussed prospects for bilateral relations, focusing on trade, investment, energy, agriculture, transport, and tourism. They also confirmed readiness to coordinate efforts within the UN and OIC.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Inviting Russia to Turkic States Organization
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has proposed inviting Russia to join the Organization of Turkic States. October 30th is recognized as International Day of Political Prisoners. The controversial film character 'Borat', who has angered Kazakhs for years, has issued an apology.

item.title: Timur Turlov and Freedom Invest Tens of Millions in Kazakh Sports
item.description: Timur Turlov and Freedom Holding Corp. have invested tens of millions of dollars in Kazakhstani sports, focusing on youth development. The Freedom QJ League, established in 2023, received over $10.71 million in the reporting period to organize competitions for youth football teams. The company also supports professional clubs and training facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Review Hemodialysis Funding Amid Rising Kidney Disease Cases
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to review its funding for hemodialysis as over 40,000 patients suffer from chronic kidney disease. The Health Ministry aims to improve dialysis care quality, enhance early diagnosis, and optimize financing. The goal is to build an effective nephrology service from polyclinics to specialized centers.
